source_review.notes: Checked current Linux man-pages documentation for io_uring overview, setup, enter and registration; POSIX AIO; Linux native AIO submission, completion and cancellation; epoll; and eventfd. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; generic request-state models, Linux-specific interfaces, illustrative execution, operational guidance and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked request tuple R, prepared, accepted, completion and freed sets, timestamp order, ring capacity relation, release/acquire publication and terminal-state transitions.
Reviewed submission, acceptance, execution, notification, completion, reaping, short I/O, cancellation, timeout, generation, backpressure and teardown terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes operation identity, resource lifetime, ring publication, interface completion and application consumption without presenting the model as an io_uring ABI.

evidence: Executed a submitted request through cancel then late-complete events.
Confirmed cancellation performs the sole terminal transition, the late completion is ignored at state canceled, and terminal count remains one.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic state machine validates one abstract arbitration order only; it invokes no AIO syscall, ring, memory barrier, device cancellation, buffer transfer or kernel work.

evidence: Re-derived that accepted operations and freed referenced state remain disjoint until terminal completion transfers ownership.
Checked prepare-before-submit-before-accept-before-complete-before-reap ordering, bounded ring occupancy and one-winner terminal transition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The sets, timestamps and state transitions are reusable reasoning models, not a formal specification of POSIX AIO, Linux native AIO, io_uring or device behavior.

evidence: Reviewed blocking, nonblocking, readiness, worker-backed, POSIX, native AIO and io_uring models; partial submission, short I/O, reverse completion, wrap, tokens, links, drains and multishot results.

Reviewed SQ and CQ exhaustion, worker starvation, registered pins and files, cancel-complete-timeout races, credential changes, restrictions, fork, exec, close, device loss, shutdown and malicious ring fields.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Semantic, identity, lifetime, memory-order, capacity, dependency, error, authority, lifecycle, performance and evidence boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced preparation, submission, acceptance, execution, CQ publication, result reaping, cancellation and teardown through twelve obligations, ten examples and five answers.

Verified unique identity, stable resources, exact accepted set, release/acquire publication, per-operation results, explicit dependencies, bounded capacity, one terminal owner and drain-before-destroy.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats ownership, ring protocol, result semantics, dependencies, resource accounting, cancellation and context lifetime as coupled but independently provable invariants.

evidence: Reviewed readiness, threads, POSIX and native AIO, io_uring rings, SQEs, CQEs, registered resources, batching, links, timeouts, cancellation, multishot, polling, workers, fairness, credentials, filesystems, sockets and shutdown.

Constructed counterexamples for nonblocking-as-AIO, submission-as-success, batch-as-full-acceptance, SQ-order-as-completion-order, slot-as-identity, cancel-as-stop, close-as-cancel and syscall-count-as-latency.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable asynchronous-I/O obligations, not a formal proof of Linux AIO, io_uring, a filesystem, driver, runtime, application or security boundary.

evidence: Audited uses of submitted, accepted, executing, completed, canceled, timed out, reaped, safe, live, ordered, bounded, supported and guaranteed.
Confirmed API contracts, abstract state machines, kernel execution paths, operational recommendations, empirical results and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Submission is not labeled acceptance, acceptance is not labeled success, cancellation request is not labeled stopped effects, and a CQE is not labeled application transaction commit.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-066/report.json records source, expected and actual event sequence, terminal state, stderr, exit status and Python version.
Reviewed required collection of token, generation, opcode, object, requested and completed bytes, timestamps, workers, results, cancellation, queue depth, overflow, registrations and lifecycle.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes only one cancel-wins arbitration; it provides no evidence for Linux AIO APIs, ring ordering, device effects, resource lifetime, security or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed readiness versus completion, AIO models, ownership, rings, publication, batching, dependencies, cancellation, registered resources, capacity, authority, lifecycle, observability and assurance as coupled concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current POSIX AIO, Linux native AIO, io_uring setup, enter, registration, SQ/CQ, linking, cancellation, polling, epoll and eventfd interfaces as implementable concerns. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from semantic models through AIO interfaces and ring mechanics, then resources, dependencies, races, capacity and shutdown, followed by twelve obligations, fourteen trade-offs, eighteen misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux AIO or io_uring maintainer, filesystem, driver, runtime, security, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
